# Healthy Banana-Oat Snack Ideas

You can make two simple, wholesome snacks from those ingredients: one baked and one pan-cooked. I’m assuming standard pantry basics like a pinch of salt and a little oil or parchment for baking.

## Two Easy Recipes

### 1) Baked Banana Oat Bars
- **Uses:** 3 bananas, 180 g oats, 2 eggs, 60 ml milk, cinnamon, 1–2 tbsp honey
- **Oven temperature:** **180°C / 350°F**
- **Method:** Mash bananas, mix with eggs, milk, oats, cinnamon, and honey. Spread into a lined baking dish and bake until set and lightly golden, about 25–35 minutes.
- **Approx. calories:** **140–170 per bar** if cut into 8 bars
- **Storage:** Cool fully, then store in an airtight container in the fridge for **up to 5 days**. Freeze for **up to 2 months**; thaw overnight or warm briefly.

### 2) Banana Oat Breakfast Cookies
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cup-hot.svg
- **Uses:** 3 bananas, 70 g oats, 1 egg, 60 ml milk, cinnamon, 1 tbsp honey
- **Oven temperature:** **175°C / 347°F**
- **Method:** Mash bananas, stir in egg, milk, oats, cinnamon, and honey. Scoop onto a lined tray and flatten slightly. Bake until firm at the edges, about 12–18 minutes.
- **Approx. calories:** **70–95 per cookie** if you make 10–12 cookies
- **Storage:** Keep in an airtight container at room temperature for **1 day** or in the fridge for **up to 4 days**. Freeze for **up to 1 month**.

## Helpful Notes
- If the batter feels too wet, add a little more oats.
- If it feels too thick, add a splash more milk.
- Very ripe bananas will give the best sweetness, so you may need less honey.
- For extra flavor, add more cinnamon on top before baking.
